html:
SMTO-LLM-0087 — The model service won't let this account use the model

GUID: a8c418e1-a5e0-426f-be58-9bdd9ff501f3
Slug: provider-access-denied
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • The model service got the request but refused permission. Your API key may be fine; the account, its access to this model, or a network rule may be blocking it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages your model service account to confirm this account may use the model named on the Main card in Settings › Setup › Model routing. This kind of refusal usually means the account or project hasn't been given access to that model.
  2. If your organization uses a proxy or firewall, ask whoever manages it whether it blocks the model service's address. Network rules can refuse requests in the same way as a missing permission.
  3. Only if they confirm the API key itself is wrong, enter the new key on the Main card, select Save Main, then select Check saved model. Replacing a key that works won't help, so change it only when it's confirmed to be the problem.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, and tasks get answers from the model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model service account. Don't replace a working API key on a guess, and don't turn off certificate checks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider returned HTTP 403 Forbidden: access was refused by account or project permissions, model entitlement, or a proxy, firewall or gateway policy, which does not by itself prove the API key is invalid.

What this means

  • The service refused access. An account permission, model entitlement, network rule or gateway policy may be responsible. This response does not prove the API key is invalid.

Why this can happen

  • The service refused access. An account permission, model entitlement, network rule or gateway policy may be responsible. This response does not prove the API key is invalid.

How to diagnose it

  • The provider returned HTTP 403 for this request.
  • The intended account can submit the same request to the selected model.

How to fix it

  • Have the provider administrator verify account and project permissions, model entitlement and any proxy, firewall or gateway policy for this endpoint and model. Replace the API key on the role card in Settings › Setup › Model routing only if it is confirmed invalid, then rerun Check saved model before resuming work.
  • Ask the provider administrator to verify account/project permissions, model access and proxy or network policy for the recorded request. Replace the key only if it is confirmed invalid.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account can submit the same request to the selected model.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
